record.paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
record.context_brief: jet drivers in Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 galaxies
record.original_question: In radio-loud Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 galaxies, which have relatively low black-hole masses yet can host powerful relativistic jets, what physical drivers launch the jets, and is jet launching controlled by the spin of the compact object or by other parameters?

evidence.quote: Especially in the radio and gamma-ray regimes, recent discoveries of relativistic jets in a fraction of NLSy1s are remarkable. The question on the nature of the physical drivers is still open.
Given the low black hole masses of these sources (MBH ∼ 106 − 108M⊙), they can be considered the ‘missing piece of unification of jets at all scales’.
Whether the jet launching is related to the spin of the compact object is not known.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies, a class of active galactic nuclei characterized by relatively narrow permitted optical emission lines (FWHM(Hβ) ≲ 2000 km/s), strong Fe II emission, weak [O III], and central supermassive black holes with masses in the range M_BH ∼ 10^6 – 10^8 M_⊙ accreting at near-Eddington rates. A small fraction of these sources are radio-loud and have been observed to launch powerful relativistic jets, detected at radio and γ-ray frequencies, despite their comparatively low black-hole masses.

Within a general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) framework for accretion onto a Kerr black hole of mass M_BH and dimensionless spin a_⋆ ∈ [0,1], with accretion rate ṁ = Ṁ/Ṁ_Edd, magnetic flux Φ threading the horizon, and host/environmental parameters Θ (e.g., disk geometry, magnetization regime such as MAD vs. SANE, host morphology, large-scale magnetic field topology):

(a) Identify the physical mechanism(s) that launch and power the relativistic jets observed in radio-loud NLSy1 galaxies. In particular, determine whether the Blandford–Znajek mechanism (extracting rotational energy of the black hole and predicting jet power P_jet ∝ a_⋆^2 Φ^2) or a Blandford–Payne–type disk-wind mechanism, or some combination, dominates jet launching in this regime of low M_BH and high ṁ.

(b) Decide whether jet launching is controlled primarily by the spin a_⋆ of the central compact object, or whether other parameters among {M_BH, ṁ, Φ, Θ} are the dominant control variables. Provide a quantitative criterion separating jetted from non-jetted NLSy1 galaxies in terms of these parameters.
artifact.category_tag: Relativistic jets in active galactic nuclei
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and studies on radio-loud NLSy1 galaxies (e.g., Berton et al. 2017; Foschini et al. 2018; Komossa et al. and follow-ups) consistently describe the physical drivers of jet launching in these low-black-hole-mass, high-accretion-rate AGN as still elusive. Black-hole spin is widely cited as a plausible jet driver via the Blandford–Znajek mechanism, but observational spin measurements in NLSy1s remain ambiguous and conflicting, and alternative drivers (magnetic flux/MAD state, accretion rate, host environment) remain viable. No consensus quantitative criterion separating jetted from non-jetted NLSy1s has been established, so the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Radio and gamma-ray loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies in the spotlight
status_evidence.snippet: Radio-loud NLS1s are unique probes of the formation of powerful radio jets at extreme (near-Eddington) accretion rates and low black hole masses.
status_evidence.claim: Jet formation in radio-loud NLSy1s remains an active research problem.

status_evidence.title: Multi-Wavelength Properties of Radio-loud Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 Galaxies
status_evidence.snippet: The mechanism of jet launching and collimation in NLS1s is still elusive.
status_evidence.claim: The jet launching mechanism in NLSy1 galaxies is not yet established.

status_evidence.title: Detection of a parsec-scale jet in a radio-quiet NLS1
status_evidence.snippet: Low BH masses and high accretion rates of NLSy1 should make them unlikely to launch jets, yet jets are observed in a fraction of them.
status_evidence.claim: Whether spin or other parameters control jet launching in NLSy1s remains open.
